items.title: Ed Allen Interview, 1961-01-14
items.q: Bob Feele on the average trumpet player, can't use that right by a piece. But he couldn't pick up anything, he just blows.

ctx.x: In the 30s? Later than that, it wasn't the last 10 or 15 years.

Was he playing in recent years? I don't know. I don't know what he's done in Chicago. He's a guy, he couldn't play, he laid his horn down for three or four weeks a month, he doesn't play, you never tell the difference, he still plays. He'd pick up anybody on the horn and play. Bob Feele on the average trumpet player, can't use that right by a piece. But he couldn't pick up anything, he just blows. And when it blows, you knew about Charlie Crescent, you never seen him, you never heard that tone. Now I'm saying…
Did you ever run into a trumpet player named George Mitchell? No I didn't. He was in Chicago all around I guess.
